Place labels around their points without overlaps

Source: R/rank_plot.R
rank_place_labels.Rd

All in inches, origin at the lower left of the panel. Each label is a box; its candidate positions are the centres of a 0.025 in grid over the panel, and the cost of a position is the gap between the point and the nearest edge of the box (at least 0.025 in). Labels are placed one at a time in `order`, each at the cheapest candidate that is inside the panel, clear of the labels placed and of all points, whose leader line passes through no label and no other point and crosses no other line, and whose box covers no line. The cost is the gap, 1.8 times higher towards the curve horizontally (`side`) and again vertically (`vside`), so that labels sit close to their points, in the corner the curve leaves empty; a box across the horizontal strip beside a point still to be labelled (on its side, at its height) costs 0.1 in more per strip, so that labels leave each other a way out and form a staircase rather than a wall. A line may cross another line (level 2, cost + 0.15 in) or pass over points (level 3, + 0.3 in) when that keeps it shorter: a short line over a point reads better than a long one across the plot. A line never passes through a label. When no candidate is clear of labels and points, labels may cover points (4), and as a last resort overlap other labels (5: the candidate overlapping them least).

Usage

rank_place_labels(
  x,
  y,
  w,
  h,
  side,
  vside,
  order,
  obs_x,
  obs_y,
  obs_r,
  self,
  panel.width,
  panel.height
)

Arguments

x, y

Positions of the labelled points

w, h

Sizes of the labels

side

1 to prefer the right of the point, -1 the left

vside

1 to prefer above the point, -1 below

order

Order in which the labels are placed

obs_x, obs_y, obs_r

Points to keep clear of, and their radii

self

Index of each label's own point among the obstacles

panel.width, panel.height

Panel size

Value

A data frame along the labels: centre (`cx`, `cy`), end of the leader line on the box (`ex`, `ey`), the `level` of the conditions met (1 = all) and the `cost` of the position, with the penalty of its level
